equities.name: TSX Composite
equities.commentary: The S&P/TSX Composite closed at 34,052, up 1.7% over the two-week period ending April 16 — the index extended its 12-month advance to 41% as energy and materials names repriced around the Strait of Hormuz crisis and its resolution24. During the first week, the benchmark gained ground as WTI spiked above US$110/bbl on supply-disruption fears; the second week saw partial reversal after the ceasefire and Strait reopening on April 17 sent crude from its peak near US$128/bbl to US$83.8540. The index sits 1.4% below its 52-week high of 34,541 set in early March 2026 and 44.3% above its 52-week low of 23,588 recorded in April 202524. Sub-index performance diverged: materials advanced on gold reaching US$4,816/oz on April 16 and copper climbing to US$6.07/lb, while financials held steady amid the seventh consecutive Bank of Canada hold17191. The Lagging Indicator cross-reference engine links the benchmark to 364 mining projects ($159.5B) and 63 oil and gas projects ($100.2B) in the database24. If the TSX holds above 34,000 amid the current BoC rate, the 211 residential projects valued at $44 billion tracked in the pipeline would continue to carry financing exposure tied to the 2-year Government of Canada yield28.

equities.name: S&P 500
equities.commentary: The S&P 500 closed at 7,022.95 on April 13, posting its best weekly gain since November at +3.9% — the advance developed as the ceasefire framework eased geopolitical risk premia and the Federal Reserve held at 3.50–3.75%, maintaining a 125–150 basis point gap above the Bank of Canada overnight rate2531. Both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq posted fresh record closes on April 1425. The index is up 25.06% year-over-year and sits 36.2% above its 52-week low of 5,158 recorded on April 21, 2025 — the first weekly close above 7,000 since late January 202626.

equities.name: DJIA
equities.commentary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 3.61% on April 9 to close at 48,185.80 — the single-session move reflected broad repricing across industrial and healthcare components as the ceasefire framework reduced the geopolitical premium embedded in energy costs25. The 30-stock benchmark is up 18.66% year-over-year and trades 4.0% below its 52-week high of 50,188 set on February 10, 2026, and 26.2% above its 52-week low of 38,170 from April 202525. The Federal Reserve signaled one rate cut in 2026 and one in 2027 at its March 18 meeting, reinforcing the wider rate differential with the BoC31. The daily gain was the largest single-session percentage advance since November 202425.

equities.name: Nasdaq Composite
equities.commentary: The Nasdaq Composite gained 4.31% on April 9 to 22,822.42, then posted a fresh record close on April 14 — technology names led the advance as falling crude prices eased input-cost pressure across the sector following the Strait of Hormuz ceasefire framework25. The index is up 33.27% year-over-year, the widest 12-month gain among the four North American benchmarks tracked, and sits 4.7% below its 52-week high of 23,958 set in late October 202525.
